introduction.text: The Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore in Rome is one of the city’s major Marian churches and a papal major basilica, renowned for its early Christian mosaics, historic relics, and role as a pilgrimage site.

history.description: Construction of the first church on the site, the Liberian Basilica, began under Pope Liberius (352–366) after a reported miraculous snowfall.
Reconstruction of the basilica under Pope Celestine I (422–432) and its consecration by Pope Sixtus III on 5 August 434.
Pope Eugene III (1145–1153) restored and extended the basilica.
Pope Nicholas IV (1288–1292) commissioned the apse mosaic of the Coronation of the Virgin.
The basilica suffered damage during the earthquake of 1348.
Pope Clement X (1670–1676) undertook interior renovations.
Pope Benedict XIV (1740–1758) commissioned Ferdinando Fuga to rebuild the façade and modify the interior.
Archaeological excavations in 1966 uncovered remains of a Roman building and an imperial calendar.
Pope Francis was buried in the basilica in 2025.

design.description: The 14th-century campanile, the tallest bell tower in Rome, rises to 246 feet.
The 16th-century coffered ceiling, designed by Giuliano da Sangallo, was gilded with gold brought by Christopher Columbus.
The façade rebuilt by Ferdinando Fuga in 1743 features a loggia and a palace-like front.
The marble columns of the nave are of Athenian origin, some dating to the first basilica.
The Marian column in Piazza Santa Maria Maggiore, erected in 1614, bears a statue of the Virgin and Child.

art.description: The 5th-century mosaics in the nave and triumphal arch depict scenes of the Virgin Mary and Christ.
The Salus Populi Romani icon, a venerated early image of the Madonna and Child, is housed in the Borghese Chapel.
The apse mosaic of the Coronation of the Virgin, completed in 1295 by Jacopo Torriti.
Frescoes by Giovanni Baglione adorn the Cappella Borghese.
The 16th-century frescoes in the Pauline Chapel were painted by Guido Reni.
